item.title: DOH-Santa Rosa Milton Office Reopens After Weather Closure
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County's Milton office will resume regular operations Thursday, October 15th after closing due to severe weather, according to a department announcement. The office had shuttered temporarily as a precaution during the weather event. Residents and patients who need health services can now contact the…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County's Milton office will resume regular operations Thursday, October 15th after closing due to severe weather, according to a department announcement.

The office had shuttered temporarily as a precaution during the weather event. Residents and patients who need health services can now contact the Milton location at 850-983-5200 to schedule appointments or inquire about available programs.

The Santa Rosa County health department provides a range of public health services to the community. No additional details about the nature or extent of the weather damage were provided in the reopening notice.

item.content:encoded:
Century is among several communities across the region still working through the aftermath of recent severe weather, according to WKRG-TV 5. Utility crews and city workers are focused on restoring electrical service and removing debris from affected areas.

The scale of cleanup efforts reflects damage across multiple neighborhoods in the city. Power restoration timelines and the scope of debris removal were not immediately detailed in early reports.

Other cities in Escambia County and the surrounding area are facing similar recovery challenges as crews prioritize reconnecting residents and clearing roadways.

item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County Sheriff's Office traffic stop led to drug charges against a man with an extensive criminal history, according to WKRG News 5.

Deputies pulled over the vehicle and a K9 unit alerted to the presence of drugs, authorities said. The arrest came during what began as a routine traffic stop in unincorporated Escambia County.

The suspect, whose name was not immediately disclosed by the Sheriff's Office, had 21 prior felony convictions on his record. Specific details about the charges he now faces were not yet available, but the drug alert from the K9 unit provided probable cause for the arrest.

item.content:encoded:
Century is still working to restore power and clear away storm damage days after severe weather swept through the area, according to reporting from WKRG News 5. Large tree limbs and fallen trees continue to clutter neighborhoods across the community, with residents describing widespread damage in their areas.

Local officials and crews are focused on both utility restoration and debris removal as the community recovers. The work is expected to continue as teams prioritize safety and access throughout affected neighborhoods.

Century is one of several communities across Northwest Florida dealing with similar post-storm challenges, including power outages and infrastructure damage.

item.title: ECAT Adjusts Routes Thursday Due to Storm Debris

ECAT will run standard service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit available from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not operate at all Thursday.…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Area Transit will resume normal operating hours Thursday, Oct. 15, but several routes will see modifications due to debris and road conditions left behind from recent weather.

ECAT will run standard service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit available from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not operate at all Thursday. Routes 45 North and 51 will skip service on Briese Lane and Ensley Street respectively, with riders directed to alternative pickup locations on Johnson Avenue and Cody Road.

The University of West Florida trolleys also will not run Thursday. ECAT warns that delays remain possible across the system due to ongoing debris on roadways, and riders should plan for extra travel time. For specifics on your route, call ECAT at 850-595-3228.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Clark, Passidomo-Smith to Florida Public Service Commission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced Wednesday the reappointment of Gary Clark and Gabriella Passidomo-Smith to the Florida Public Service Commission, a regulatory body that oversees the state's utility companies. Clark, of Chipley, has served as a PSC Commissioner since 2017. Before that role, he worked as Deputy Secretary of Land and Recreation for…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Wednesday the reappointment of Gary Clark and Gabriella Passidomo-Smith to the Florida Public Service Commission, a regulatory body that oversees the state's utility companies.

Clark, of Chipley, has served as a PSC Commissioner since 2017. Before that role, he worked as Deputy Secretary of Land and Recreation for the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and served on the Washington County School Board, Chipola College District Board of Trustees, and the Northwest Florida Water Management District Governing Board. He holds a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Phoenix.

Passidomo-Smith, based in Tallahassee, has been a PSC Commissioner since 2021. She previously worked as an attorney in the Regulatory Analysis Section of the PSC's Office of the General Counsel and sits on committees within the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners focused on gas utility regulation and pipeline safety. She earned her bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Florida and a juris doctor from Washington and Lee University School of Law.

Both appointments are subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate.

item.title: Navarre Beach lifts boil water notice after safety testing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County has rescinded a boil water notice for all Navarre Beach Utilities customers after bacteriological testing confirmed the water is safe to drink, according to a county announcement Wednesday afternoon. The notice, which had required customers to boil water before consumption, was lifted following completion of required safety…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County has rescinded a boil water notice for all Navarre Beach Utilities customers after bacteriological testing confirmed the water is safe to drink, according to a county announcement Wednesday afternoon.

The notice, which had required customers to boil water before consumption, was lifted following completion of required safety surveys. Santa Rosa County did not specify how long the notice had been in effect or what prompted the initial precaution.

Other water utilities in Santa Rosa County remain under boil water notices, including the City of Milton Water, Town of Jay, Bagdad, and Garcon Point Water. Customers of those systems should continue to boil water until further notice from the county.

item.title: Community Health Northwest Florida Palafox clinic reopens Thursday after Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Community Health Northwest Florida will reopen its North Palafox Street location tomorrow, Thursday, October 15, after power was restored to the facility. The clinic at 1400 N. Palafox Street will resume full services including adult and family care, walk-in appointments, pharmacy, lab work, and X-ray services. The reopening is part of the…
item.content:encoded:
Community Health Northwest Florida will reopen its North Palafox Street location tomorrow, Thursday, October 15, after power was restored to the facility. The clinic at 1400 N. Palafox Street will resume full services including adult and family care, walk-in appointments, pharmacy, lab work, and X-ray services.

The reopening is part of the organization's broader recovery following Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall on October 9. According to a statement from the health center, most of its 14 locations across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties have already resumed operations, with services expanding throughout the week. Reopened sites include the Jackson Street main clinic, the Milton location, and pediatric clinics at Trinity, Highway 90 in Pace, and Cantonment.

Three locations remain offline due to power outages: 12th Avenue Pediatrics and school-based clinics at Pine Forest High School and C.A. Weis Elementary. The organization said it's working to move patient appointments from closed sites to facilities that are operational. Escambia County schools remain closed through October 16.

"Our staff adapted above and beyond," said Community Health Northwest Florida CEO Chandra Smiley in the announcement. Patients needing to refill prescriptions or with other questions can call 850-436-4630, and the health center said it will continue posting updates on its website and social media accounts.

item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Early voting for the 2026 General Election in Santa Rosa County will begin Monday, October 19, and run through October 31, the county announced. All six early voting sites will operate from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. during that period. County officials are asking voters to be patient as recovery work continues on roads and around voting locations following…
item.content:encoded:
Early voting for the 2026 General Election in Santa Rosa County will begin Monday, October 19, and run through October 31, the county announced. All six early voting sites will operate from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. during that period.

County officials are asking voters to be patient as recovery work continues on roads and around voting locations following recent storm damage. The early voting sites include the Main Elections Office in Milton, locations in Gulf Breeze, Pace, Navarre, and two Milton facilities. Vote-by-mail ballots can also be dropped off at any early voting location during those hours.

Voters needing more information can visit www.votesantarosa.gov or call the Santa Rosa County Supervisor of Elections Office at 850-983-1900 to find the location nearest them.

The notices were initially issued following a water system issue affecting the utility's distribution network.

The suspect is now in custody facing robbery and assault charges related to the incident. The sheriff's office did not immediately release additional details about the business targeted or the extent of injuries sustained by the deputies involved.

item.title: Escambia County Warns Hurricane Victims to Check Contractors, Permits Before Repairs
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Escambia County officials are warning Hurricane Isaias victims that rushing into home repairs with an unlicensed contractor could create problems long after the storm cleanup is finished. Escambia County Building Services and Permitting Director Tim Tolbert says homeowners should verify contractors are properly licensed and…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Escambia County officials are warning Hurricane Isaias victims that rushing into home repairs with an unlicensed contractor could create problems long after the storm cleanup is finished.


Escambia County Building Services and Permitting Director Tim Tolbert says homeowners should verify contractors are properly licensed and insured before allowing work to begin.

One warning sign can be an advertisement or work vehicle that claims a contractor is licensed without displaying a license number.

Tolbert said Florida-licensed contractors are required to include that number in their advertising.


Homeowners should also get a written contract detailing the work and its cost, seek multiple bids when possible and be cautious of demands for large upfront payments or cash.

Tolbert stressed another distinction that can easily become confused during hurricane recovery: Escambia County has waived storm-repair permit fees, not permit requirements.

Required permits must still be obtained.


Failing to do so can create problems later, including complications with insurance coverage or the sale of a home.


County officials say homeowners should also photograph damage before cleanup and retain contracts, receipts and other documentation related to hurricane repairs.

Suspected unlicensed contracting can be reported to Florida's Unlicensed Activity Hotline at 866-532-1440.


These six give the website a good mix rather than making the homepage entirely hurricane logistics: power/accountability, schools/accountability, water/service, relief/resources, community response and consumer protection.

item.title: Senator Moody Pushes for More Florida National Guard Troops After Isaias Response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody is calling on the Department of War to increase the number of Florida National Guard personnel allocated to the state, citing the gap between the growing population and the stagnant size of the Guard. The effort comes in the wake of Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall in Florida last week and activated roughly 5,000 Guard…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody is calling on the Department of War to increase the number of Florida National Guard personnel allocated to the state, citing the gap between the growing population and the stagnant size of the Guard. The effort comes in the wake of Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall in Florida last week and activated roughly 5,000 Guard soldiers and airmen for rescue, recovery, and humanitarian assistance operations.

Moody is joined by 13 U.S. Representatives from Florida in the push for increased allocations, including Aaron Bean, Gus Bilirakis, Vern Buchanan, and others. "While Florida's population has grown in recent years, the size of our National Guard has not kept pace," Moody said in a statement. "We need to make sure they have the personnel and resources to continue answering the call."

During the Isaias response, Guard members performed route clearance, reconnaissance, flood mitigation, and search-and-rescue work across the state. In one notable operation, eight Florida National Guard soldiers rescued a family from a sinking pickup truck beside an Interstate 10 off-ramp. Moody and Governor Ron DeSantis conducted an on-the-ground damage assessment after the storm to thank Guard members for their efforts.

item.title: Navy Federal, Hancock Whitney Announce $200,000 in Hurricane Recovery Donations
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Two major employers with Northwest Florida ties have announced a combined $200,000 in donations to support Hurricane Isaias recovery. Hancock Whitney announced Tuesday that it would contribute $100,000, with $50,000 going to United Way of West Florida and another $50,000 to United Way of Emerald Coast. Navy Federal Credit Union…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Two major employers with Northwest Florida ties have announced a combined $200,000 in donations to support Hurricane Isaias recovery.


Hancock Whitney announced Tuesday that it would contribute $100,000, with $50,000 going to United Way of West Florida and another $50,000 to United Way of Emerald Coast.

Navy Federal Credit Union announced Wednesday morning that it is donating another $100,000 to United Way of West Florida's Hurricane Isaias Relief Fund.

The announcements were made separately.


Hancock Whitney Northwest Florida Market President Bruce Vredenberg said the bank chose United Way because of the organization's existing relationships with agencies providing assistance to hurricane victims.


Vredenberg said the longer-term needs of storm victims were also a consideration.

“The real story is what goes on and lingers beyond that,” Vredenberg told NewsRadio 92.3, pointing to needs that may not be covered by FEMA or other government assistance.

Navy Federal said its donation will support emergency assistance and longer-term recovery for families in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.


The hurricane has a particularly close connection to Navy Federal's local workforce. The credit union says nearly 95% of employees in its Greater Pensacola Operations live in Escambia or Santa Rosa County.


Vredenberg encouraged other businesses and individuals to contribute whatever they can toward the recovery.

item.title: Convoy of Hope Brings More Than 350,000 Pounds of Hurricane Relief Supplies to Region
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Convoy of Hope says it has brought more than 350,000 pounds of relief supplies into communities affected by Hurricane Isaias and plans to continue distributions throughout the week as long as residents need assistance. The humanitarian organization has been operating in the region since Friday, providing food, bottled water, baby…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Convoy of Hope says it has brought more than 350,000 pounds of relief supplies into communities affected by Hurricane Isaias and plans to continue distributions throughout the week as long as residents need assistance.


The humanitarian organization has been operating in the region since Friday, providing food, bottled water, baby supplies, hygiene products, tarps, storage totes and other necessities.

Relief operations are serving communities including Pensacola, Pace, Gulf Breeze, Century, Jay and Niceville in Florida, along with Brewton and East Brewton in Alabama.

Demand has been substantial.


Convoy of Hope says more than 800 people came through its Pace distribution site Tuesday alone, with hundreds of vehicles using distribution sites throughout the affected region over the past several days.


Ethan Forhetz, vice president of Convoy of Hope, said teams plan to remain in Northwest Florida throughout the week as long as residents continue needing supplies.


Individual distribution locations and operating hours can vary. Residents should confirm current site information before traveling to a distribution point.

item.title: Escambia County Emergency Officials Credit Prior Disaster Experience for Faster Hurricane Response
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County's emergency management team deployed lessons learned from previous disaster responses to speed up operations as Hurricane Isaias impacted the Florida Panhandle, according to Public Safety Director Eric Gilmore. Gilmore told InWeekly that sending county staff to assist with recovery efforts in other parts of Florida following recent…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County's emergency management team deployed lessons learned from previous disaster responses to speed up operations as Hurricane Isaias impacted the Florida Panhandle, according to Public Safety Director Eric Gilmore.

Gilmore told InWeekly that sending county staff to assist with recovery efforts in other parts of Florida following recent storms has significantly improved the department's readiness and coordination capabilities. The hands-on experience gained from those deployments has translated into sharper planning and faster mobilization when disasters strike locally.

The approach reflects a broader regional strategy where counties share resources and expertise during hurricanes and other emergencies, allowing emergency managers to anticipate challenges and streamline response protocols.
